articles.title: Curtis Jones set to leave Liverpool as Inter submit £30m offer for midfielder
articles.summary: Homegrown star has been longstanding target for Italians. Jones in the final year of his contract at Anfield. Inter have submitted an offer of €30m rising to €35m (£30m) for Curtis Jones, with the Liverpool midfielder expected to leave his boyhood club after a 16-year association.
body: Liverpool valued their homegrown midfielder closer to €40m but, with Jones in the final year of his contract and no sign of an agreement over an extension, that figure is unlikely to be reached.

Intermediaries representing Inter contacted Liverpool in July with a proposal to pay up to €35m for Jones. Negotiations between the clubs commenced on Wednesday. No agreement has been reached but, with Inter willing to go up to €35m, Liverpool are likely to sanction Jones’s departure. Inter’s willingness to pay Tottenham €35m for Djed Spence last week is seen as a benchmark figure for the Jones deal.

Jones, who has played six times for England, has been at Liverpool since the age of nine, but has been unable to secure a regular first-team starting role and cut a frustrated figure at times last season under Arne Slot.

Andoni Iraola, Slot’s replacement as head coach, spoke at his unveiling about the importance of keeping the Toxteth-born midfielder and of having a local identity in his team. But Inter’s determined pursuit and the risk of losing the player on a free transfer next summer have also to be factored in by Liverpool.

articles.title: Fifth Fifa vice-president turns against Infantino, saying he has ‘lost confidence’ in him
articles.summary: Hungary’s Sandor Csanyi highly critical of Fifa president. He cites dismissal of COO Kevin Lamour as ‘final straw’ Gianni Infantino has lost the support of another one of Fifa’s vice-presidents, with the Hungarian football federation chief, Sandor Csanyi, criticising the president’s “professional…
body: In an explosive letter sent to Infantino on Tuesday, which was first obtained by the news agency Agence France-Presse, Csanyi states that he has “lost the confidence I previously placed in you” and describes the “unexpected dismissal” of Fifa’s chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, as the “final straw”.
Lamour was sacked by Fifa on Monday after breaking ranks last month by criticising Infantino over his aborted plan to sell off shares in the World Cup to private investors.
Csanyi’s letter continues the trend of senior global football figures deserting Infantino, with the Hungarian banker the fifth of Fifa’s eight vice-presidents to call for him to stand down.

The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, Victor Montagliani of Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean Confederation – and Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al Khalifa of the Asian Football Confederation have all made their positions clear, as has the Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt.

articles.summary: Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue both took five-wicket hauls to put England in early control of the opening Test against Pakistan at Headingley, as the home side closed on 112-2 at stumps on day one, just 59 runs behind the tourists' first-innings total of 171.

articles.title: Tongue and Robinson’s high fives put England in control against Pakistan
articles.summary: First Test day one: Pakistan 171; England 112-2. Root (37*) and Cox (23*) add 64 to leave deficit of 59. For all that Joe Root was playing his 167th Test match for England, and had led the side on 65 previous occasions, there will surely have been a few butterflies as he pulled on the blazer and…
body: Root was resuming what he once described as an “unhealthy relationship” with the captaincy, while a supposedly one-off return to the job earlier this summer ended in a crushing defeat to New Zealand. Aged 35, England’s premier batter could easily have said a polite “no thank you” when the vacancy came around again.

Yet Root appears to be driven by something more than just duty; a sense of unfinished personal business, perhaps. And if there were any nerves or second thoughts, they surely evaporated once Ollie Robinson struck with the first ball of the series to set in motion a one-sided opening day against Pakistan.

By stumps the match had progressed significantly. Robinson went on to claim his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket with a masterful display of wobble seam, while Josh Tongue picked up his fourth to share all 10. And in response to Pakistan’s 171 all out in 48.1 overs, England closed on 112 for two from 25, with Root 37 not out.

articles.title: Edmonton Marathon admits 2026 route was more than half a kilometre too long
articles.summary: Canadian contest sparked outrage from scores of frustrated runners online and in Canadian media. The organisers of the Edmonton Marathon have admitted the course was more than half a kilometre too long, after outrage from scores of runners who complained about the distance.
body: The error resulted in the upending of runners’ personal bests and potentially prevented some from breaking records.

Participants who were hoping to use Edmonton as a qualifier for the Boston Marathon may have also faced disappointment, as mere seconds can make the difference between being accepted or denied a spot in the prestigious race. Many runners are drawn to the Edmonton race for a chance to gain entry to Boston.

After a cascade of frustrated runners voicing their concerns online and in Canadian media, race organisers had initially said the course was officially certified and undoubtedly the correct distance. But in statements on Tuesday, they admitted a mistake was made.
“We do not take this lightly,” said race director, Tom Keogh. “We hosted the nation’s best athletes and their finishing times did not truly reflect their amazing performances,” he said.

articles.title: Robinson & Tongue give Root an ideal start to England's new era
articles.summary: Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue each take five wickets to give Joe Root the ideal start to his second spell as England captain as Pakistan are skittled for 171 on the opening day of the series at Headingley.
body: Returning four years after his first stint as skipper left him and his team broken, Root's leadership was barely tested thanks to the excellence of his bowlers and fragility of the Pakistan batting.
Root won the toss, pounced on the opportunity to bowl first and Robinson set the tone by pinning Azan Awais leg before with the first ball of the match.
Robinson expertly exploited the movement on offer, relentlessly hitting a full length for his 5-51.
Tongue took longer to warm to his task but when he also found the correct length, he was also too much for Pakistan to handle. Tongue's 5-46 ended with a final devastating burst of 4-5 from 11 balls.

articles.summary: Parents should not be scared their children might not come back from a cycling race following the death of Finlay Tarling, Lorena Wiebes says after winning the opening stage of the Tour of Britain Women.
body: Dutch cyclist Lorena Wiebes (SD Worx - Protime) sprinted to take the opening stage in Cockermouth.

Before the race began, there was a touching tribute to the British 19-year-old who died last week in a high-speed collision with a van, which had strayed on to the road during the eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.

As the 114 riders lined up to set off on the first stage in Cockermouth, a photograph of Tarling was projected on to a large screen and a minute's applause rang out around the packed centre of the market town.
After her win, Wiebes said: "Most of these riders have family at home. Your parents shouldn't be scared that you are not coming back from a race.

articles.summary: New Cliftonville director Conor Devine says Champions League nights at Solitude are "not too far away" after the Toronto Investment Group‘s takeover of the club.
body: New Cliftonville director Conor Devine believes Champions League nights at Solitude are "not too far away" after the Toronto Investment Group‘s [TIG] takeover of the club.
Cliftonville members voted in favour of a TIG takeover on Monday, and the group have said they will invest £3million in first 36 months.
TIG will have a 90% share of the 147-year-old club, with the remaining percentage retained by the membership.
"We make no bones about it, this is not a plaything for us, this is an amazing opportunity," Devine told BBC Sport NI's Thomas Kane.

articles.title: England skittle Pakistan at Headingley on Root's return as Test captain
articles.summary: Joe Root's second spell as England Test captain began with his side skittling Pakistan for 171 at Headingley as Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue each bagged five-wicket hauls around a lengthy rain delay and a brief fightback from the tourists.
body: Root is back in charge following Ben Stokes' shock international retirement in June and charged with turning around the team's fortunes after seven defeats and just one win in their last 10 games, across fixtures against India, Australia and New Zealand.

Bar wet weather preventing any play from 11.50pm-1.45pm, and Abdullah Shafique (61) and Imam-ul-Haq (42) putting on a stand of 91 from 6-2, this was an excellent day for Root, with Pakistan rolled in 48.1 overs before the hosts closed on 112-2 in reply, trailing by 59.

England lost Ben Duckett (15) lbw and Emilio Gay (33) caught at slip, to Mohammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali respectively, leaving Jordan Cox (23no) - into the side at No 3 in place of the injured Jacob Bethell - and Root (37no) to usher the side to the 7.30pm stumps with an unbroken stand of 64.
The day had been extended after the earlier rain, which could return in droves on day two.

articles.title: Masters, Webb criticise FIFA over Balogun red card controversy
articles.summary: Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban.
body: Richard Masters, the chief executive of the Premier League and Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer in England, say the decision undermines faith in football at all levels of the game.
Balogun was sent off in the last 32 match against Bosnia & Herzegovina which led to an automatic ban under World Cup rules, without the opportunity for appeal, or for the ban to be reduced.
However, US president Donald Trump then called FIFA president Gianni Infantino to complain, which led to the decision being overturned and Balogun was allowed to play against Belgium in the last 16.

Webb said: "I was really troubled by it. I don't know the ins and outs of the process, but what we know is: a red card was shown. You can form an opinion about the validity of the red card, I can understand why it was given.
